brief: The canvas displays a textured, aged paper surface upon which time is measured by the organic blooming of liquid ink. Concentric patterns of black and colored ink spontaneously bleed outward, spreading into the porous fiber structure of the newsprint. These vibrant, dendritic blooms move slowly and continuously, creating ephemeral stains and ephemeral voids. The entire composition is a visual study of diffusion, where the only observed movement is the relentless, unpredictable spread of liquid pigment across the stationary paper.

statement: This sketch depicts the slow, organic diffusion of mineral deposits across crystalline steel strata in a desert gorge. The composition shows rust-colored formations that slowly expand and contract in undulating waves, creating an illusion of movement through static elements. Each stratum is rendered with multiple concentric circles to simulate the spreading of minerals through porous surfaces, while subtle texture lines add depth and visual complexity. The continuous animation captures the patient, relentless process of geological change, where only the boundaries of these formations shift over time. The color palette emphasizes earth tones and metallic rusts, evoking the harsh beauty of desert landscapes where mineral deposits slowly seep through steel-like structures.
